title: The OODA Loop
author: The Good Boss
summary: A decision-making framework adapted from U.S. Air Force Colonel John Boyd's combat strategy, the OODA Loop—Observe, Orient, Decide, Act—teaches leaders to cycle through information processing faster and more deliberately than the chaos around them. The framework emphasizes that faster adaptation requires not just speed but deliberate intention. Leaders who can observe facts clearly, interpret them in context, decide on their best move, and act while immediately looping back to observe consequences stay ahead of uncertainty. The key: cycle through the loop with intention, not panic.
points: OODA (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act) was born in fighter pilots' survival strategies and applies to any leader facing fast-moving uncertainty.
The faster you cycle through the loop with intention, the more you adapt, respond, and stay ahead.
Orientation—interpreting what you've observed in context—is as critical as raw observation.
Speed without deliberation becomes panic; speed with intention becomes leadership advantage.
quotes: The pilots who could process new information faster, and act on it, had the edge. They weren't necessarily the strongest or most experienced. They were simply better at staying ahead of the situation.
What makes it different from other models is speed. The goal is to cycle through the loop faster and better than the chaos around you.

And here's what I like most about this model: The faster you go through the loop with intention, the more you can adapt, respond, and stay ahead.” Archived from The Good Boss on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
